newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Goldman Sachs sees more activity, no office in NZ.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs sees more activity, no office in NZ.

text.p: United States investment bank Goldman Sachs said on Thursday it expects to develop activity in New Zealand but has no plans to open an office here in the foreseeable future, the New Zealand Press Association reported.

The company announced the appointment of two prominent Australian businessmen, Malcolm Turnbull and Neville Wran as chairman and managing director of Goldman Sachs Australia and New Zealand on Tuesday and said it was seeking to grow its Asian business.

Goldman Sachs head of investment banking operations in Australia and New Zealand David Livingstone told NZPA on Thursday that Australasia was now part of Asia. The mature investment banking markets in New Zealand and Australia would be key parts of the platform of the bank' growth in the region.

"I would expect our business going forward in New Zealand to be like the Goldman Sachs investment banking business anywhere focusing on mergers and acquisitions advice and debt and equity raising particularly international ones in the United States and European markets," he said.
"At this stage we cover the Australasian region from a single office in Sydney. I don't expect that to change in the near term."
In New Zealand, Goldman Sachs has advised Tranz Rail. It also advised Prudential, when purchasing NZI Life from General Accident, and Freightways on its disposal of courier businesses.
It also advises large local corporates on debt funding and when seeking dual stock exchange listings in New Zealand and the United States.
